properties.name: BASELINE — one server holding one 202-node / 2.9 MB design sits at 448 MB resident, and no cause for that is established
properties.statement:
MEASURED 2026-09-13 BY FLO2'S SESSION, not by this one, and relayed by @ajs in conversation. Release binary, --serve-shared, one store open, holding a 202-node / 2.9 MB design:

    VmRSS 448 MB · VmHWM 473 MB

Reproduce with: grep -E '^(VmRSS|VmHWM)' /proc/$(pgrep -f 'reflow2-mcp.*serve-shared')/status

WHAT THE NUMBER IS ODD AGAINST: 2.9 MB of design, 448 MB resident — roughly 150x. That ratio is the reason this is written down rather than filed as a tuning preference.

🛑 NO CAUSE IS ESTABLISHED HERE, DELIBERATELY. The explanation offered with the reading — that all six column families in ALL_CFS take Options::default(), so six write buffers at 64 MB is ~384 MB of memtable before anything else, and only nodes and edges even get a block-based table factory — is ARITHMETIC READ OUT OF crates/reflow2-core/src/foundation/store/backend.rs (cf_options(), RocksBackend::open()). flo2's own session says so in as many words: "the causal claim above is arithmetic from source, not yet a measurement." It is the first plausible explanation and it has not been put to anything that could refute it. Recording it as the cause would be exactly the move the root-cause discipline exists to stop, so it is recorded as a HYPOTHESIS and no CAUSES edge is drawn.

WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT: change one setting at a time on the same design and re-read, rather than all three at once. Write throughput must be watched on the way down — this trades memory for it.

ALSO NOT ESTABLISHED: how much of the 448 MB is per-process and how much is per-open-store. One process with one store is one point on a line. ver:the-per-open-design-cost-is-measured is the measurement that separates them.
